column1: # Cover search providers - read by concat-audio and convert-audio when nothing
# local gave a book or a long track a cover.
# This is the shipped table. To change it, copy it anywhere, edit the copy and
# point the coverSearchTable setting at it.
# One TAB-separated row per search, five columns. Blank lines and # lines are
# ignored. The rows are tried top to bottom among those whose content matches,
# and the first image a row finds is the cover: put the searches you trust most
# first.
# The columns:
#   content   what the audio probably is: podcast, drama, audiobook, music,
#             classical or other. A file name ending in a [YouTube id] -
#             yt-dlp's default - or starting with a yyyymmdd date, or a length
#             from 30 to 200 minutes, reads as a podcast - but 30 to 200
#             minutes in stereo reads as a drama, since a talk is encoded
#             mono. Anything longer reads as an audiobook; a shorter one as
#             other. Whatever its length, a genre tag that is not speech, or
#             a folder called Music on the way to it, reads as music - and a
#             classical genre, a conductor, a catalogue number such as
#             "Op. 27" or a folder called Klassik reads as classical.
#   provider  how the answer is read: audible, amazon, deezer, itunes,
#             musicbrainz (its front cover from the Cover Art Archive),
#             openlibrary or youtube. A new site needs a reader in medialib/lib/onlinecover.py;
#             a new address for a known one only needs a row.
#   match     how sure the answer has to be:
#               id      none: the address names the very video the file came
#                       from, by the {youtube_id} in its name.
#               strict  the title, and nothing that contradicts it - an author
#                       or channel, a running time - and at least one of those
#                       agreeing when the title alone is short.
#               loose   the title alone: another edition, another language, or
#                       the printed book instead of the audiobook.
#               show    the podcast's own name, for the show's artwork rather
#                       than the episode's.
#               performer  a classical release: its artist is the
#                       recording's performer, and its title names the work
#                       - with whatever else the record couples it with.
#                       Where the folder names a label - "35 Lindqvist
#                       (Nordlabel, 1972)" - only that label's release, by
#                       the copyright line a site gives (iTunes does).
#   pace      seconds between two requests to this provider, at least.
#   address   the request. {title}, {creator}, {query} (both together),
#             {episode} (what follows the last " - " of a name in parts:
#             "Series - Episode 6 - Its Title"), {youtube_id}, and for music
#             {work}, {performer} and {composer} are filled in, URL-encoded; a row that needs one the file does not have is
#             passed over. youtube's address is handed
#             to yt-dlp: a ytsearchN: search, or a watch address.
# podcast: the video the name's id points at, when it has one - only the
# thumbnail download failed; else the episode searched on YouTube, where it
# usually came from; then the show's artwork.
podcast
